title: Contextual Remediation Blueprint Composer for Privileged Ops
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Build a 'Blueprint Composer' that converts incident context and telemetry into safe, auditable remediation task bundles for privileged operational workflows. The composer should: 1) infer candidate remediation recipes from incident metadata (alerts, high-cardinality traces, last successful run), 2) surface typed parameters with validation and least-privilege defaults, 3) provide a sandbox dry-run mode with simulated side effects, and 4) generate an execution plan that is RBAC-gated and produces structured audit records suitable for compliance review. The output is a runbook-as-task bundle (sequence of typed steps, rollback actions, preconditions) that can be executed by the admin CLI, Console, or via the Ops API. Focus areas: safety harness (approval gates, idempotency tokens), telemetry events (remediation.attempt|success|rollback|dryrun), and tight integration with existing runbook templates and oncall routing. This ticket covers MVP back-end composer, CLI integration, and telemetry hooks; Console UX will be follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: Composer takes a JSON incident payload and returns a parameterized remediation bundle with typed inputs and rollback definitions
Dry-run mode executes in sandbox cluster and returns simulated diffs without making changes
RBAC gating: steps that require privileged credentials are flagged and require a one-time approver token; attempts are logged
Telemetry emits remediation.attempt, remediation.outcome, and remediation.rollback with correlation_id
End-to-end example reproducible via CLI and CI test harness; integration tests added
Design doc and security review completed and linked

Land PR #14321 behind feature flag in staging and run synthetic remediation scenarios
Add end-to-end tests that exercise dry-run sandbox and real execution with canary limits

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental privileged execution — Mitigation: default dry-run + mandatory approver token for privileged steps
Risk: ambiguous parameter bindings leading to destructive ops — Mitigation: typed schema + least-privilege defaults + preview diffs
Risk: noisy telemetry and alerts — Mitigation: sampling for repeated automated remediations and backpressure on event emission
